correctness.rationale: The spin-flip generator gives an exact closed ODE for the sum of spins for each finite ring. Pareto alpha>1 provides finite-mean nonlattice renewal epochs and exact stationary age density. The log-coordinate change of variables is bijective with positive Jacobian. The derivative of log density has signs lambda and lambda-alpha/a, proving the complete cutoff-dependent modal classification. The coarse and exact laws agree outside a disjoint sector of mass p, giving exact TV p. The explicit coupling is monotone and optimal for W1 by the 1-Lipschitz identity witness; its transport integral is evaluated exactly. The actual embedded verification program completed 210 parameter/quadrature/sampling tests. No finite experiment is used as a proof of the continuum assertions.

value.rationale: For a current Pareto-reset Ising magnetization model, the published stationary cutoff-atom component changes the qualitative measure type and near-reset peak. The exact b=alpha boundary determines when that finite secondary mode really exists, while a sharp TV error p persists regardless of small cutoff width even as W1 vanishes linearly. This resolves an explicitly motivated approximation-interpretation problem and quantifies whether observers sensitive to atoms or only Lipschitz observables can treat the coarse law as accurate. It does not purport to create new general renewal theory.
